newsitem.title: GERMANY: Countries having second thoughts on Zaire - Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: Countries having second thoughts on Zaire - Kinkel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday several countries which wanted to take part in a military mission to eastern Zaire were now having second thoughts.
He told reporters a meeting to discuss a possible military component for an international rescue operation in the region had been postponed and would take place on Friday.

A foreign ministry spokesman later said Kinkel's remarks about the meeting, originally scheduled for Wednesday, had been based on press reports and that it was up to U.S. military authorities in Stuttgart to make an official announcement.
A spokesman at the U.S. European command in Stuttgart, scheduled to host the meeting, said it would make an announcement on the talks later on Wednesday.
Kinkel said the subject of military involvement had also been discussed on Tuesday at a meeting of Western European Union in the Belgian port of Ostend.

"At that time the impression was that an international aid force would be necessary. Obviously some of the countries who wanted to take part have had somewhat different thoughts in the meantime," he said.
Kinkel did not say to which countries he was referring. Germany is not expected to send any troops.
Kinkel said the military meeting had been postponed to allow another round of political talks to take place in New York.

Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien had already said the Stuttgart meeting would probably be delayed until Friday. His foreign minister Lloyd Axworthy said the political meeting would be held on Wednesday.

Kinkel, speaking before a meeting with aid organisations, said it was vital the international community continued to provide as much humanitarian help as possible, regardless of any decision about a military mission to Central Africa.
He thanked Germans for donating generously to aid organisations helping in the region.
"There can be no doubt that the situation is extremely critical and that help must be given," he said.
"I'm proud of what has been done by the aid organisations in this region. I've seen it with my own eyes and I'd like to thank all those who are working there."
International agencies have said the situation in the region is still critical, even though hundreds of thousands of refugees have now left eastern Zaire to return home to Rwanda.
